extracted.intended_audience: prospective authors, journal editors, and peer reviewers in academic psychiatry / medical research
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of common reasons manuscripts are rejected at a specialty medical journal (Indian Journal of Psychological Medicine), intended to inform authors, reviewers, and editors about avoidable and fatal flaws across submission, peer-review, and editorial-re-review stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of novelty/originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript topic or research question does not add sufficient new knowledge or originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most common reason for desk rejection (≈51.8% of desk rejections). Judgement of novelty has subjectivity; authors can improve perceived novelty by addressing specific limitations of prior studies and clearly arguing how their work advances the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Out of scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter does not fit the journal’s defined scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common cause of desk rejection (17.4% of desk rejections). Authors should match manuscript topic to journal scope (e.g., journal title may imply boundaries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper study design for the stated objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The chosen study design is inappropriate to answer the research question (e.g., using cross-sectional design to make causal claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design flaws are often fatal and lead to rejection; ensure study design aligns with objectives and avoids designs that cannot support claimed inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of control group
rubrics_metrics.description: Study lacks an appropriate control or comparison group where one is required to test the hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of control can be a fatal methodological flaw; consider study designs that include controls or justify alternatives robustly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor control of confounders
rubrics_metrics.description: Insufficient measurement or statistical control of confounding variables that bias results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common design-related reason for rejection; plan data collection and analysis to identify and adjust for key confounders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obsolete or weak methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of outdated, inappropriate, or weak methods for the research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological choices should be current and fit-for-purpose; justify methods and, if possible, reference contemporary approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical issues (lack of informed consent/assent/IEC approval)
rubrics_metrics.description: Absence of requisite ethics committee approval or informed consent processes for human-subject research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics-related errors are considered fatal; obtain and report IEC/IRB approvals and consent procedures prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Unattributed copying or overlap with previously published text or data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plagiarism is an ethics violation and grounds for rejection; ensure originality and proper citation; use plagiarism checks before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: No CTRI registration (for intervention trials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to register clinical trials in the Clinical Trials Registry of India (CTRI) when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For interventional trials, prospective registration is required; lack of registration is an ethics/registration error that can lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneous submission of the same manuscript to multiple journals or redundant publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplicate submission violates editorial policies and may lead to rejection and sanctions; submit to one journal at a time and disclose related submissions/publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor elaboration of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods section lacks sufficient detail or clarity to evaluate study conduct or reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A major reason for post-peer-review and editorial rejection (methods inadequately elaborated in ~50.7% of post-peer-review rejections). Provide detailed methodology, including sampling, measures, procedures, and analysis plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Unclear, unintelligible, or unscientific language and presentation of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poor writing was often cited (≈45.2% post-peer-review). Improve clarity, organization, and language; seek editorial help or senior author assistance when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor presentation of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Results are presented inadequately — unclear tables/figures, repetition, or poor organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure results are clearly and succinctly presented with appropriate tables/figures and avoid unnecessary repetition between text and tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement errors / incorrect choice of instruments or measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of inappropriate, invalid, or poorly chosen measurement instruments or errors in measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorrect or invalid measures are often fatal; select validated instruments suitable for the population and outcome and justify choices in the methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrong conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions are not supported by the data or overstate the findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstating implications; align conclusions with results and discuss limitations and alternative explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors in data analysis — multiple comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to account for multiple comparisons leading to inflated type I error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply appropriate corrections or pre-specify analyses; reviewers commonly flag multiple comparisons issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors in data analysis — improper tests for stated objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of inappropriate statistical tests that do not match the study design or hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose statistical tests appropriate to data types and design; consider consulting a statistician and report rationale for test selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long delay for submitting comments on published article (letters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters commenting on published articles submitted beyond the journal's stipulated timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some journals have strict windows (e.g., two months) for letters; adhere to timelines when submitting comments on published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor quality review articles — non-systematic
rubrics_metrics.description: Review submitted as a narrative when the topic warrants a systematic review or when systematic methods are expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For topics requiring comprehensive synthesis, conduct and report systematic review methods; mis-specified review type can lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor quality review articles — poor synthesis of findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of critical synthesis or integration of the literature; mere description without analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good reviews critically synthesize and evaluate evidence; include methods for literature search and critical appraisal when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestions for technical modifications not followed despite repeated reminders
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors fail to implement requested technical fixes after reminders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to and implement requested technical/modification suggestions promptly; failure to do so can result in rejection without peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small sample size / power/sample size issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Insufficient sample size or inadequate power to detect meaningful effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design studies with appropriate sample size calculations and justify sample adequacy; small samples are a common fatal/problematic issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection due to hugely delayed revisions by the authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors' long delays in returning revisions lead to rejection, especially when data recency becomes a concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to revision requests in a timely manner; excessively delayed revisions may make findings less relevant and invite rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion section fails to contextualize findings, compare with recent literature, or address limitations adequately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide balanced interpretation, relate results to existing evidence, acknowledge limitations, and avoid repeating results in the discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak study rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Insufficient or unconvincing justification for why the study was undertaken or why it matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame a clear, evidence-backed rationale in the introduction, highlighting gaps the study addresses and its potential contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitted as narrative review when topic is more suitable for a systematic review
rubrics_metrics.description: Author chooses a narrative approach for a topic better addressed by systematic review methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the question requires systematic methods; if so, follow established systematic-review reporting standards (e.g., PRISMA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate literature survey
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to include recent, relevant literature in background or discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct a thorough, up-to-date literature search and cite key recent studies to justify the study and place findings in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of critical synthesis of the findings from the literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Review/manuscript fails to critically synthesize existing evidence, merely listing studies without analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically appraise and integrate past findings, identify patterns, and explain how the current work advances understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper inclusion/exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Inappropriate or poorly defined inclusion/exclusion criteria that bias sample selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and justify inclusion/exclusion criteria clearly; ensure they align with the research question and avoid introducing selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Research question is poorly framed, unclear, or inappropriate for the chosen design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulate a clear, answerable research question that aligns with design and analyses; poor questions can be fatal to manuscript acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification: Fatal versus non-fatal flaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between flaws central to study validity (fatal) and those fixable during revision (non-fatal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fatal flaws include errors in framing the research question, major study-design defects (improper design, wrong instruments, lack of control group) and ethics lapses—these are typically unfixable post hoc. Non-fatal flaws (e.g., overstated results, some statistical errors, inadequate discussion) may be corrected during revisions.
